questions.problem: The first term of an arithmetic series is ${a}_{1}=5,$ the common difference is $d=-2.5,$ and the sum of the series is ${S}_{N}=-105.$ Find the number of terms $N$ in the series.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the number of terms, we can use the following formula:

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d).
$$

We substitute ${a}_{1}=5$, $d=-2.5$ and ${S}_{N}=-105$ into the above and solve for $N$, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ -105 & =\frac{N}{2}(2\cdot 5+(N-1)\cdot (-2.5)) \\ -210 & =N(10-2.5N+2.5) \\ -210 & =12.5N-2.5{N}^{2} \\ 2.5{N}^{2}-12.5N-210 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

For the equation above, the quadratic formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}N & =\frac{-(-12.5)\pm \sqrt{(-12.5)^{2}-4\cdot 2.5\cdot (-210)}}{2\cdot 2.5} \\  & =\frac{12.5\pm 47.5}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $N=12$ or $N=-7.$ We disregard the negative solution since $N$ must be positive.

Therefore, our series has $N=12$ terms.

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d)\,\,
$$

We have been given the sum ${S}_{N}=470,$ and the first term ${a}_{1}=2.$ Our goal is to find $N,$ the number of terms.

The common difference $d$ can be found, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =2.5-2 \\  & =0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these values into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 470 & =\frac{N}{2}(2(2)+(N-1)(0.5)) \\ 940 & =N(4+0.5N-0.5) \\ 940 & =N(0.5N+3.5) \\ 940 & =0.5{N}^{2}+3.5N \\ 0.5{N}^{2}+3.5N-940 & =0 \\ {N}^{2}+7N-1\,880 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

For the equation above, the quadratic formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}N & =\frac{-7\pm \sqrt{(-7)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot (-1\,880)}}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{-7\pm \sqrt{7\,569}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-7\pm 87}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $N=40$ or $N=-47.$ We disregard the negative solution since $N$ must be positive.

Therefore, our series has $N=40$ terms.

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d)
$$

Since we know two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{5}-{a}_{1}}{5-1} \\  & =\frac{5-(-3)}{4} \\  & =\frac{8}{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 192 & =\frac{N}{2}(2(-3)+(N-1)(2)) \\ 192 & =\frac{N}{2}(-6+2N-2) \\ 192 & =\frac{N}{2}(2N-8) \\ 192 & =N(N-4) \\ 192 & ={N}^{2}-4N \\ {N}^{2}-4N-192 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

For the equation above, the quadratic formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}N & =\frac{-(-4)\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot (-192)}}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{784}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 28}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $N=16$ or $N=-12.$ We disregard the negative solution since $N$ must be positive.

Therefore, our series has $N=16$ terms.

Now, substituting $a_1=4,$ $d=2.5,$ and $S_N=850$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 850 & =\frac{N}{2}(2(4)+(N-1)(2.5)) \\ 850 & =\frac{N}{2}(8+2.5N-2.5) \\ 850\cdot 2 & =N(5.5+2.5N) \\ 1700 & =2.5{N}^{2}+5.5N \\ 2.5{N}^{2}+5.5N-1\,700 & =0 \\ 5{N}^{2}+11N-3\,400 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

For the equation above, the quadratic formula gives

$$
\begin{aligned}N & =\frac{-(11)\pm \sqrt{(-11)^{2}-4\cdot 5\cdot (-3400)}}{2\cdot 5} \\  & =\frac{-11\pm \sqrt{68\,121}}{10} \\  & =\frac{-11\pm 261}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

So $N=25$ or $N=-27.2.$ We disregard the negative solution since $N$ must be a positive integer.

Therefore, our series has $N=25$ terms.
